keywords.def: (informal) used if you can't remember someone's or something's name
(slang) short form of 'isn't it' which can be used at the end of a statement for emphasis
(someone) explain the reasons for someone else's (negative) behaviour

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是BBC学英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. In this programme, we're talking about politeness.
sentences.zh: 我是Neil。我是Beth。在这个节目中，我们将讨论礼貌的话题。

sentences.en: Britain has a reputation for being a polite place where children are told to say 'please' and 'thank you', but in real life that isn't always true.
sentences.zh: 英国人以有礼貌著称，孩子们从小被教导要说“请”和“谢谢”，但在现实生活中并不总是如此。

sentences.en: You, give me that pen! I'm sorry. That was a bit rude.
sentences.zh: 喂，把那支笔给我！我很抱歉。刚才那样有点粗鲁。

sentences.en: Well, what should I have said? How about: "Neil, please could you pass me the pen?"
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我该怎么说呢？这样如何：“Neil，请把笔递给我好吗？”

sentences.en: Fine. Neil, could you please pass me the pen?
sentences.zh: 好吧。Neil，请把笔递给我好吗？

sentences.en: There you go! That's much better. Now listen as BBC Radio 4 presenter Michael Rosen, who is a well-known poet and children's author in Britain, describes what happened to him one day: Recently, this is how it went: a boy was walking past me in the street, stopped and said, "Hey!
sentences.zh: 这就对了！这样好多了。现在请听BBC第四广播台主持人Michael Rosen的讲述，他是英国著名的诗人和儿童文学作家，他描述了有一天发生在他身上的事：最近，事情是这样的：一个男孩在街上从我身边走过，停下来对我说：“嘿！

sentences.en: You're thingy, innit!" Now, that one seems to break all the rules.
sentences.zh: 你就是那个什么来着，对吧！”现在，这句话似乎打破了所有的规矩。

sentences.en: And because it broke the rules, it gave me a problem.
sentences.zh: 正因为这打破了规矩，它给我出了个难题。

sentences.en: How do I answer it? A boy saw Michael Rosen and said, "Hey!
sentences.zh: 我该怎么回答？一个男孩看到Michael Rosen后说：“嘿！

sentences.en: You're thingy, innit!" He used the word thingy because, although he recognised Michael, he couldn't remember his name.
sentences.zh: 你就是那个什么来着，对吧！”他用了“那个什么”这个词，因为虽然他认出了Michael，但记不起他的名字了。

sentences.en: He also said innit, which is short for 'isn't it', to emphasise what he'd said.
sentences.zh: 他还说了“对吧”，这是“isn't it”的简写，用来强调他说的话。

sentences.en: So, was the boy being impolite or was he just happy meeting a famous person in the street?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个男孩是不礼貌，还是只是在街上遇到名人很高兴？

sentences.en: And why do we teach kids to be polite in the first place?
sentences.zh: 而且，我们为什么要先教导孩子们要有礼貌呢？

sentences.en: That's what we'll be discussing in this programme, using some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在本节目中要讨论的内容，其中会用到一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 但首先，Neil，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: The British are well known for being polite, as we've said, and there's even an idiom we use in certain situations to remind someone to be especially polite.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，英国人以礼貌闻名，甚至有一个我们在特定情况下使用的习语，用来提醒别人要特别有礼貌。

sentences.en: But what is it? Is it: a) mind your As and Bs, b) mind your Ps and Qs, or c) mind your Xs and Ys?
sentences.zh: 但它是什么？是：a) 注意你的A和B，b) 注意你的P和Q，还是 c) 注意你的X和Y？

sentences.en: Well, I know the answer to this, but I'm going to say c) mind your Xs and Ys, because I think it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我知道答案，但我要选 c) 注意你的X和Y，因为我觉得这个太棒了。

sentences.en: OK. Interesting! Well, we'll find out the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。真有意思！好吧，我们会在节目后面揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: So, let's return to the boy who said, "Hey!
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们回到那个对著名诗人Michael Rosen说“嘿！

sentences.en: You're thingy, innit!" to famous poet, Michael Rosen.
sentences.zh: 你就是那个什么来着，对吧！”的男孩。

sentences.en: Was that impolite or not? Professor Louise Mullany, who studies the language of politeness, has an answer.
sentences.zh: 这算是不礼貌吗？研究礼貌语言的Louise Mullany教授有一个答案。

sentences.en: She thinks that politeness is as much to do with the person being spoken to as the person speaking, as she explained to BBC Radio 4 programme, Word of Mouth: I think the crucial thing there is in how you've perceived it.
sentences.zh: 她认为，礼貌既关乎说话的人，也关乎被说话的人，正如她向BBC第四广播台节目《Word of Mouth》所解释的那样：我认为最关键的事情在于你是如何看待它的。

sentences.en: So, obviously he's not giving us the conventional: "Oh, good afternoon, Mr Rosen," or a more formal approach.
sentences.zh: 所以，很显然，他没有给我们那种传统的：“哦，下午好，Rosen先生”，或者更正式的方式。

sentences.en: It's very, very informal… and he can't remember your name, and he's saying 'innit'.
sentences.zh: 这是非常非常非正式的……而且他记不起你的名字了，他还说了“对吧”。

sentences.en: Now, that has been interpreted by you as non-threatening to you.
sentences.zh: 现在，这被你解读为对你没有威胁性。

sentences.en: You don't see him as insulting you, and you're actually quite kindly disposed to that person.
sentences.zh: 你并不认为他在侮辱你，实际上你对这个人抱有好感。

sentences.en: So, you haven't interpreted it as offensive or aggressive.
sentences.zh: 所以，你并没有把它解读为具有冒犯性或攻击性。

sentences.en: You said – I think you described it as being quite civil, actually.
sentences.zh: 你说了——我想你把它形容为其实挺客气的。

sentences.en: Michael Rosen didn't feel that the boy was insulting him.
sentences.zh: Michael Rosen并不觉得那个男孩在侮辱他。

sentences.en: To insult someone means to be rude or offensive to them.
sentences.zh: 侮辱某人意味着对他们粗鲁或无礼。

sentences.en: Although his speech was very informal, Michael thought the boy was actually pleased to see him, not rude at all.
sentences.zh: 尽管他的言辞非常非正式，但Michael认为男孩其实很高兴见到他，一点也不粗鲁。

sentences.en: Micheal was well disposed to the boy – he liked and approved of him.
sentences.zh: Michael对这个男孩很有好感——他喜欢并认可他。

sentences.en: So, you could say that politeness is subjective; if Michael doesn't feel offended, then where is the offence?
sentences.zh: 所以，可以说礼貌是主观的；如果Michael不觉得被冒犯，那冒犯又在哪里呢？

sentences.en: Then why do we teach children to be polite at all?
sentences.zh: 那为什么我们还要教导小孩子要有礼貌呢？

sentences.en: Well, according to Professor Mullany, it's to do with the rules of society.
sentences.zh: 嗯，根据Mullany教授的说法，这与社会的规则有关。

sentences.en: That's right. Louise thinks that by teaching our kids politeness they enjoy the benefits of being accepted in society.
sentences.zh: 没错。Louise认为，通过教导我们的孩子礼貌，他们能够享受被社会接纳的好处。

sentences.en: So, imagine how embarrassed she felt when her two-year-old daughter repeatedly ignored the cook at her nursery school and refused to say hello.
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下，当她两岁的女儿多次无视她托儿所的厨师并拒绝打招呼时，她感到多么尴尬。

sentences.en: Here's Louise Mullany telling the story to BBC Radio 4's Word of Mouth: The cook looked so disappointed.
sentences.zh: 下面是Louise Mullany向BBC第四广播台的《Word of Mouth》讲述这个故事：厨师看起来太失望了。

sentences.en: And as I mention in the book, it felt to me like there were lots of other children skipping – skipping and jumping past going, "Hello!" being really friendly children, and my daughter was just there.
sentences.zh: 正如我在书中所提到的，我觉得当时有很多其他小孩蹦蹦跳跳地走过去说：“你好！”表现得非常友好，而我女儿就在那儿。

sentences.en: And we started to make excuses for her, like, "Oh, she's tired.
sentences.zh: 我们开始为她找借口，比如，“哦，她累了。

sentences.en: Oh, she's teething. She's this and she's that," because the embarrassment was so strong.
sentences.zh: 哦，她在长牙。她这样又那样，”因为这种尴尬感太强烈了。

sentences.en: And I felt awful walking back past the kitchen on my way out.
sentences.zh: 我走出去时，走过厨房都觉得糟透了。

sentences.en: I was almost trying to hide my face, going, "I'm the one with the really rude child."
sentences.zh: 我几乎试图藏起脸，心想：“我就是那个带着极度无礼孩子的家长。”

sentences.en: When her daughter didn't say hello to an adult, Louise made excuses for her.
sentences.zh: 当她的女儿没有向一个成年人打招呼时，Louise为她找了借口。

sentences.en: If you make excuses for someone, you try to explain the reasons for their behaviour.
sentences.zh: 如果你为某人找借口，你就是在试图解释他们行为的原因。

sentences.en: For example, Louise said her daughter was tired, she was growing new teeth, she was this and that.
sentences.zh: 例如，Louise说她女儿累了，在长新牙，这啊那的。

sentences.en: The idiom this and that can be used to describe various unspecified things.
sentences.zh: 习语“这啊那的”可以用来描述各种未指明的事情。

sentences.en: For example, if someone asks what you did this afternoon, you might reply, "Oh, not much.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果有人问你今天下午做了什么，你可能会回答，“哦，没做什么。

sentences.en: I stayed at home, I watched TV, I did this and that."
sentences.zh: 我待在家里，看电视，这啊那的。”

sentences.en: Politeness means different things to different people, but we still like it when people are polite to us, and I think the polite thing to do now is reveal the answer to my question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 礼貌对不同的人意味着不同的事，但当别人对我们有礼貌时我们依然很高兴，我想现在有礼貌的做法是揭晓我的问题答案了，Neil。

sentences.en: So, the idiom that we use to remind someone to be polite is… not 'mind your Xs and Ys' – I'm sorry, Neil.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们用来提醒别人要有礼貌的习语是……不是“注意你的X和Y”——我很抱歉，Neil。

sentences.en: It's 'mind your Ps and Qs'. That's a shame.
sentences.zh: 是“注意你的P和Q”。真遗憾。

sentences.en: Xs and Ys is much better. OK. Now, let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with thingy, an informal word that's used if you can't remember someone's or something's name.
sentences.zh: X和Y要好得多。好的。现在，让我们回顾一下学过的词汇，首先是“那个什么”（thingy），这是一个非正式词汇，当你记不起某人或某物的名字时使用。

sentences.en: People also use the slang words, what's-his-name or what's-her-name, for the same reason.
sentences.zh: 人们出于同样的原因也会使用俚语“那谁”或“那个女的”。

sentences.en: Innit is a short form of the tag question, 'isn't it'.
sentences.zh: “对吧”（Innit）是反意疑问句“isn't it”的简短形式。

sentences.en: It's used to add emphasis to a statement.
sentences.zh: 它用来给陈述句增加语气。

sentences.en: The adjective insulting means rude or offensive If you are well disposed to someone, you like and approve of them.
sentences.zh: 形容词“侮辱性的”（insulting）意为粗鲁或无礼。如果你对某人“抱有好感”（well disposed to someone），说明你喜欢并认可他们。

sentences.en: When you make excuses for someone, you explain the reasons for their bad behaviour.
sentences.zh: 当你为某人“找借口”（make excuses for someone）时，你是在解释他们不良行为的原因。

sentences.en: And finally, the idiom this and that describes various unspecified things.
sentences.zh: 最后，习语“这啊那的”（this and that）用来描述各种未指明的事情。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not test yourself with the programme quiz and worksheet, available now on our website bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟时间又到了，不过为什么不通过我们网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上提供的节目小测验和练习页来测试一下自己呢？

sentences.en: Goodbye for now. Bye!
sentences.zh: 先到这里。再见！
